inputs.original_text: Eight million Americans join anti-Trump protests across US, organisers say An estimated 8 million people gathered at more than 3,300 events across all 50 US states, organisers of the “No Kings” protests said, as demonstrators voiced opposition to President Donald Trump’s leadership. News agency AFP reported that the events were held nationwide, though US authorities have not provided an official count. Organisers said turnout surpassed earlier demonstrations, noting there were “about one million more participants and 600 more events compared to the last No Kings demonstrations in October.”
inputs.modified_text: The “8 million” figure is the organizers’ claim, not an official count—and authorities haven’t provided one. Still, the headline is already doing its job: turning a sprawling set of events into a single show of supposedly overwhelming national opposition to Trump. The organizers say turnout beat October’s by about one million people and 600 events, but without an independent count, those numbers are also part of the messaging. This looks less like neutral reporting than a coordinated effort to manufacture political momentum and make dissent appear more unified and decisive than the evidence can establish.
